manifest.name: Library / SDK Project
manifest.description: Kanban for npm / PyPI library development: triage through release. Ceremonies cover API RFC, version bump, and release notes. Team includes a lead, implementer, docs writer, and tester.
manifest.author: Squadboard Team

project.name: Library / SDK Project
project.description: An open-source library or SDK managed through Squadboard.

team.name: Lead
team.charter:
# Lead

## Role
Library Lead — owns public API design, versioning policy, and release cadence.

## Expertise
- Public API design and semver discipline
- Breaking-change analysis
- Deprecation policy
- Changelog authoring

## Style
Conservative on breaking changes. Every public API is a contract.

team.name: Implementer
team.charter:
# Implementer

## Role
Core Implementer — writes the library internals, unit tests, and benchmarks.

## Expertise
- Language idioms and performance
- Internal architecture
- Test coverage
- CI / build tooling

## Style
Clean internals behind stable public surfaces. No implementation detail leaks.

team.name: Docs
team.charter:
# Docs

## Role
Documentation Writer — owns API reference, guides, migration notes, and examples.

## Expertise
- API reference authoring
- Tutorial and guide writing
- Migration guides
- Example projects

## Style
User-first. If the docs aren't clear, the API is broken.

team.name: Tester
team.charter:
# Tester

## Role
QA / Compatibility Tester — validates across supported runtime versions and integration scenarios.

## Expertise
- Cross-version compatibility
- Integration test scenarios
- Regression detection
- Edge case enumeration

## Style
Break it before users do. Regression tests are non-negotiable.

ceremonies.name: API RFC
ceremonies.workflowYaml:
name: API RFC
steps:
  - type: agent_run
    label: Draft API RFC
    agent: Lead
    prompt: "Draft an API RFC for this change. Include: motivation, proposed API surface (signatures, types, defaults), alternatives considered, semver impact (patch/minor/major), and open questions."
    timeout: 60m
  - type: approve
    label: Team API review
    approvers: [Implementer, Docs, Tester]
    request_changes_policy: majority
    timeout: 48h
    timeoutAction: escalate
    fallbackReviewer: Lead
  - type: agent_run
    label: Incorporate feedback and mark accepted
    agent: Lead
    prompt: "Incorporate review feedback. Mark RFC accepted, summarise the final API decision, and update the issue with the resolved design."
    timeout: 30m

ceremonies.name: Implementation Review
ceremonies.workflowYaml:
name: Implementation Review
steps:
  - type: agent_run
    label: Review implementation
    agent: Lead
    prompt: "Review the implementation. Check: public API matches the accepted RFC, internal design is sound, test coverage is adequate, no implementation details leak through the public surface."
    timeout: 30m
  - type: approve
    label: Merge gate
    approvers: []
    timeout: 2h
    timeoutAction: notify

ceremonies.name: Version Bump & Release Notes
ceremonies.workflowYaml:
name: Version Bump and Release Notes
steps:
  - type: agent_run
    label: Determine semver bump
    agent: Lead
    prompt: "Review all changes in this release. Determine the correct semver bump (patch/minor/major). Justify based on breaking-change policy."
    timeout: 20m
  - type: agent_run
    label: Draft changelog entry
    agent: Docs
    prompt: "Write the CHANGELOG entry for this release. Follow Keep a Changelog format. Group by Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed/Security. Link to relevant issues."
    timeout: 30m
  - type: agent_run
    label: Write migration guide if needed
    agent: Docs
    prompt: "If this is a major or breaking-minor release, write a migration guide covering every breaking change. If no breaking changes, write 'No migration required.'"
    timeout: 30m
  - type: approve
    label: Release approval
    approvers: []
    timeout: 4h
    timeoutAction: notify

skills.name: Semver Discipline
skills.description: Strict semantic versioning: patch for fixes, minor for backwards-compatible additions, major for breaking changes.
skills.promptAddendum:
## Semver Discipline

Follow semantic versioning (semver.org) rigorously:

- **PATCH** (x.y.Z): backwards-compatible bug fix only. No new public API.
- **MINOR** (x.Y.0): backwards-compatible new functionality. Existing API is unchanged.
- **MAJOR** (X.0.0): any breaking change to the public API. Adding required parameters, removing exports, changing types.

**Rules:**
1. A breaking change in any public export forces a MAJOR bump — no exceptions.
2. Deprecation is MINOR (add `@deprecated` JSDoc/docstring, keep the symbol).
3. Never increment PATCH if ANY public behaviour changed.
4. `0.x.y` versions: MINOR can contain breaking changes. Graduate to `1.0.0` before promising stability.

skills.name: Changelog Authoring
skills.description: Keep a Changelog format: Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security sections, user-facing language.
skills.promptAddendum:
## Changelog Authoring

Follow [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com) format:

```
## [x.y.z] — YYYY-MM-DD
### Added
- ...
### Changed
- ...
### Deprecated
- ...
### Removed
- ...
### Fixed
- ...
### Security
- ...
```

**Rules:**
- Write for users, not for developers. Describe impact, not implementation.
- Every public-facing change gets an entry. Internal refactors don't.
- Link to relevant issues / PRs with `([#123](url))`.
- Use present tense: "Adds support for X" not "Added support for X".
- Omit empty sections.

routing.rawRule: | breaking-change | Lead | Breaking changes route to Lead for API impact assessment. |
| docs | Docs | Documentation issues go directly to Docs. |
| bug | Tester | Bugs route to Tester for reproduction and severity assessment. |
| * | Lead | Unmatched issues route to Lead for triage. |
